name: Elmsfeuer
prior: Closest prior appeared three weeks ago: Hügelton Nikolator (27 Sep 2026, macOS/Windows, pay-what-you-want from 1 USD) - a physical-modelling synth of a musical Tesla coil that 'models the resonant circuit, the electrical discharge, and the sound that discharge makes in the air', with voltage, current, discharge, arc length, branching, drive envelope; CPU-heavy because it runs far above audio rate (VS: blog.dubspot.com/hugelton-nikolator-2026, matrixsynth.com 2026/09 nikolator). Hardware: Gamechanger Audio PLASMA Voice (Eurorack, real high-voltage discharges in a xenon tube driven by an ultrasonic PWM oscillator, monophonic; VS: synthtopia.com/?p=140043, modulargrid). Real singing arcs: ArcAttack/Zeusaphone ('crisply distorted square wave sound', tone from the spark modulated at the note; VS: en.wikipedia.com/wiki/ArcAttack, bobbyowsinskiblog Zeusaphone), 2009 singing-Tesla-coil emulator toy (VS: boingboing.net 2009/05/15), Chalmers 'Singing Arc' thesis (VS: odr.chalmers.se 254868); Duddell 1899 (A). Crackle/hum: freesound Jacob's-ladder recordings (hum tied to mains, 'the hum of the 60Hz arc'; VS: freesound.org/712004) and generic noise/crackle plugins (A); no app or plugin found that offers hum -> corona crackle -> arc as one control under a finger (two searches, one extended, zero hits). Myzel: Tiefe = tanh growl on sine+octave (APP 4394-4460) overlaps the hum stage when the hum sits on f; Schwarm = FM chaos. Rare: electric arcs exist as physical model (Nikolator) and as hardware (Plasma Voice), not as a touch-playable voltage ladder.
costNotes: Native: hum (osc + asymmetric WaveShaper 'none' + HP + drift gain = 4) + crackle (noise, LP, dead-zone WaveShaper, HP, gain = 5) + arc (saw osc, 2 looped BufferSources for steps/gates, 2 gains, BQ, WaveShaper, gain = 8) + out ~ 18 nodes x 0.03 = 0.55 plus 3 WaveShapers at oversample 'none' (curve lookup ~ a gain and a half each, A) and 2 BQ premiums -> ~0.7 with the arc chain live; ~0.45 with Bogen = 0 (idea's 0.75 is right). L3 (two arcs L/R, 2x shapers, second crackle) ~1.35. Use oversample 'none' everywhere: WaveShaper 2x costs ~8-10 biquads per channel (R: webaudio.md section 7) and would double the voice. No worklet needed: all three stages are k-rate-controllable native chains; the arc pitch steps as a looped AudioBuffer into osc.detune is the app's driftBuf pattern (APP 2818-2836) and sums with the v.mod bus. Dead-zone crackle: density follows LP cutoff and drive, output is sparse clicks - cheap and correct. Caveat: a 2 s step/gate loop is audibly periodic within 4 s; per-voice random loopStart/playbackRate (0.9-1.1) breaks it for free.
soundHeld: Bottom: a hum at fold(f) (30-120 Hz) under the note - unmistakably 'mains' only when it sits at a fixed low pitch; if 'Netz' puts it on f it becomes a tanh-driven harmonic buzz = Tiefe's growl with even harmonics (clone risk, must default to fold). Middle: lowpass-noise through a dead-zone = Geiger/vinyl-style crackle whose density grows with y - good, physical, recognisable as corona. Top: a sawtooth two octaves up, bandpassed and tanh'd, gated by a stutter buffer, with fifth/octave/fourth jumps from a loop: this is the laser/sci-fi risk the idea names; with a fixed 30-120 ms step pattern it reads as a 'robot arpeggio' rather than an arc. What saves it: the arc must stay noisy (bandpass on the crackle, not only on the saw; crackle gates the arc, not a loop), the jumps must be sparse (< 3/s) and the hum must continue underneath. Held, the column is genuinely two instruments (drone / lead) which is musically rich but means a single note never has one timbre - the Hoehe axis is a register switch, not a continuous timbre, which breaks Myzel's held-note convention (Hoehe = colour) unless the transition zone (Spannung 0.4-0.7) is wide and the arc fades in with increasing density rather than switching. Bebung = Netzflattern is a nice reading of the detune bus. Pitch identity is strong at the hum (if on f) and at the arc; crackle alone has no pitch - the middle register is noise.
soundBurst: The strongest of the four as a hit: Zündstoß + 0.22 s zap + crackle tail is a percussive, electric, instantly recognisable 'Zap' that Puls lanes and Sporenregen can use at any tempo (0.002 s attack, 0.15 s release); velocity scales both level and arc reach. Risk: at 1/16 notes a sawtooth zap with the same pitch steps every hit is a machine gun; randomise the step buffer offset per hit and tie the step depth to vel.
failureModes: Arc = cheap laser: fixed step loop, pure saw, bandpass Q 2 -> 'robot arpeggio'; needs crackle-driven gating, sparse jumps, noise in the arc and hum underneath.
Hum on f = Tiefe clone (tanh growl with even harmonics); default must fold to 30-120 Hz and let the arc/corona carry the note.
Hoehe is a register switch (drone -> noise -> lead), not a continuous timbre; needs a wide crossfade zone, or the held-note convention breaks and Gestik tilt flips registers.
2 s loop buffers (steps, gates, crackle) repeat audibly; per-voice random offsets and playbackRate jitter required.
DC and sub-30 Hz from asymmetric shaping (HP 30 Hz specified; also keep the asymmetry small or the mixer meters pin).
Middle register (crackle only) has no pitch; chords of corona are static noise beds - document as texture.
Cost 0.7 x three fingers plus a Puls lane = 2.8 units of 14 on a phone for one timbre family; arc chain must really be lazily built.
verdict: Rare: the arc itself now exists as a physical model (Nikolator, released 27 Sep 2026) and as hardware (Gamechanger Plasma Voice, ArcAttack coils), but nobody offers mains hum -> corona crackle -> singing arc as one finger axis in a touch instrument, and the Zap is a Puls hit no Myzel engine has. Native-feasible at ~0.7 units (L3 ~1.35) with oversample 'none' and lazy arc construction; the step/gate loop buffers are the app's driftBuf pattern. Held it is two instruments under one column, which is musically rich but turns Hoehe into a register switch rather than a timbre, and the arc stage is one bad default away from a 1990s laser patch - it survives only if crackle gates the arc, jumps stay sparse, and the hum folds to 30-120 Hz instead of sitting on f (where it becomes Tiefe). As a burst it is the best of the four: a percussive electric zap with a crackle tail at any tempo. Build it, with the arc design treated as the risky part and auditioned early.
